planting.note: Root stem cuttings in moist, well-drained, humus-rich potting mix in bright indirect to partial shade; give it a mossy support to climb so it develops leaf fenestrations.

directions: This 2026 Costa Farms introduction is a fenestrating pothos with dark green leaves heavily streaked and splashed in gold variegation, winner of National Garden Bureau's People's Choice Green Thumb Award. Grown vertically on a support it readily punches fenestrations into its young leaves and can eventually produce mature leaves nearly two feet long; left to trail, foliage stays smaller and climbs or cascades six feet or more. It tolerates lower indoor light and some drought once established but colors up and grows fastest with brighter indirect light, and it should be watered as the top two inches of soil dry.
sources: Costa Farms (costafarms.com) — Yellow Sunrise product page

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in well-drained, chunky, humus-rich mix; provide a sturdy pole or support and bright light close to an east- or west-facing window for best color.

directions: Golden Compact is a newer, award-winning selection of the familiar Swiss cheese plant, part of Costa Farms' Trending Tropicals collection and winner of TPIE 2026's Favorite Trending Foliage Award. Instead of the usual solid dark-green leaf, its foliage is an even, zesty lime-green rather than blotched or marked, and its petioles hold the leaves unusually close to the main stem for a tidier, more compact silhouette than a standard Monstera deliciosa. As leaves mature they enlarge and develop the classic Monstera slits and holes, with brighter, more saturated color in stronger light; it reaches six feet or more with support over time.
sources: Costa Farms (costafarms.com) — Monstera Golden Compact product page

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in well-drained, humus-rich mix near an east- or west-facing window; give it a support to climb so leaves enlarge and fenestrate.

directions: Named for Krabi Province, Thailand, this is a hard-to-find Epipremnum pinnatum selection Costa Farms says it is among the only North American growers offering. Its long, narrow, medium-green leaves are delightfully variegated with silver streaks, and the plant can be grown either as a trailing houseplant or trained to climb, with leaves enlarging and developing Monstera-like slits and fenestrations as it ascends a support. It tolerates low light and average home humidity but performs best above 60°F with occasional moisture checks, going dry between waterings roughly every one to two weeks.

planting.note: Plant in containers or in-ground after frost danger passes in full sun with one to two hours of afternoon shade in hot climates; fertilize monthly for best bloom.

directions: Flora is a new-for-2026 large-flowering tropical hibiscus bred by Graff Breeding, named TPIE 2026's Favorite Trending Flowering Plant. Its blooms open creamy white with a soft pink center and some ruffling and can exceed seven inches across, and the breeder claims it reblooms faster than other large-flowered tropical hibiscus while branching more heavily so flowers form at many new growth tips. Individual blossoms are also unusually long lasting, holding up to four days in cool weather versus roughly one day for typical tropical hibiscus varieties. It performs equally well in containers or planted in-ground and is a thirsty, heavy feeder, needing at least six hours of direct sun and consistently moist soil.
sources: Costa Farms (costafarms.com) — HibisQs Flora product page

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in well-drained, humus-rich mix placed three to four feet from an east- or west-facing window; tolerates lower light but colors best in bright indirect light.

directions: This Costa Farms selection of Scindapsus sp. Platinum form shows off large, almost heart-shaped, soft green leaves entirely frosted in silver, distinguishing it from other Scindapsus forms that are mottled with green or show a dark central midrib. It can be grown trailing from a shelf or basket, or trained to climb and trail more than five feet. It needs checking weekly and watering whenever the top two inches of soil dry, going about one to two weeks between waterings.
sources: Costa Farms (costafarms.com) — Scindapsus Platinum Java product page

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in well-drained, humus-rich mix within three feet of an east- or west-facing window; give it a support to climb for larger, more fenestrated leaves.

directions: A newly offered Epipremnum pinnatum selection with green leaves heavily splashed in creamy white for a marbled look, with each leaf uniquely patterned. Its leaves are longer and narrower than Marble Queen Pothos and develop eye-catching marginal slits and fenestrations that give a climbing plant a Monstera-like appearance, with mature leaves exceeding eighteen inches when grown vertically on a support to six feet or more. It tolerates medium light but grows more slowly in lower light, and prefers to dry out somewhat between waterings roughly every one to two weeks rather than staying consistently wet.
sources: Costa Farms (costafarms.com) — Epipremnum pinnatum Marble product page
